items.basis: The claimed mechanism accounts for numerous complex physical phenomena but fails to address the fundamental electrochemical reaction pathways that dominate grid corrosion during float charge, as evidenced by the absence of any discussion on the Pb/PbO2 transformation kinetics in the provided evidence bundle.

The specified boundary condition of continuous float charge at 2.27V per cell is insufficiently narrow, as research (doi:10.1109/intlec.1995.498976) demonstrates that corrosion rates are highly sensitive to voltage variations within the 2.2-2.3V range, which the candidate fails to account for.

The candidate's prediction of a 20% reduction in grid cross-section reduction rate directly contradicts the findings in doi:10.1109/intlec.1995.498933, which establishes that under float charge conditions, corrosion rates follow a logarithmic relationship with time rather than being linearly reducible through geometric modifications.

The candidate's novel design variable (porous electrode structure geometry) cannot overcome the fundamental limitation that increased porosity reduces mechanical strength, as acknowledged in the known failure modes, making the solution equivalent to the baseline in terms of long-term structural integrity.

The proposed numerical solution cannot be practically implemented due to the computational complexity of simultaneously modeling all claimed phenomena (excluded-volume effects, local pressure variation, etc.) while maintaining acceptable simulation times for industrial design cycles, as evidenced by the absence of such implementations in the referenced literature.

The testable prediction fails to specify measurement methodology for grid cross-section reduction rate, particularly regarding how to distinguish between corrosion-induced cross-section loss and mechanical degradation due to the acknowledged failure mode of reduced mechanical strength from increased porosity.
